messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: GPU pool 'eu-west-1-pool-a' saturated (queue depth 12k, reject rate 41%). Autoscaler failing to scale: repeated cloud API 429/504s and hit configured scale_limit=80 nodes. Paging rotation: oncall Alex (20m)
Alex: I'm on it — joining bridge. initial checks: dashboard shows sustained enqueue rate ~300 req/s and average seq_len bumped by customer batch job. Can someone confirm failures are autoscaler-related vs cloud provisioning?
Riley: I see autoscaler logs showing rapid scale_up attempts then immediate backoff. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:01:12Z scaler: ScaleUp(5)->request sent
2026-03-15T02:01:12Z cloud-api: 429 Too Many Requests
2026-03-15T02:01:13Z scaler: backoff 60s
2026-03-15T02:01:45Z scaler: ScaleUp(5)->request sent
2026-03-15T02:01:45Z cloud-api: 504 Gateway Timeout
2026-03-15T02:01:46Z scaler: failed, retry count 3
2026-03-15T02:02:00Z scaler: scale_limit reached (80)
```
Riley: autoscaler is also refusing to enqueue more attempts after hitting scale_limit. That looks like a config + cloud throttle combo.
Mira: Runtime telemetry shows many long-lived KV cache holds from a few large embedding jobs — those sessions pin gpus longer than normal. Also see a surge of batch requests from tenant `partner-x` at 01:55 UTC.
Jen: Platform: we're seeing provider-side rate limiting in the eu-west region; provider team reports transient allocation pressure. We have some spare capacity in eu-central and us-west.
Alex: Initial mitigation plan: 1) Apply admission control to reduce new low-priority jobs by throttling non-prod tenants; 2) Route traffic for high-SLA tenants to fallback model (smaller model) / different region; 3) If safe, raise scale_limit temporarily to 120 while we coordinate provider. Starting step 1 now.
Sam: I've posted a customer advisory to CS we should send to impacted customers if we see >5% errors. Elaine, want to coordinate comms?
Elaine: Yes. Please tag me when you have a short impact summary. I'll prepare a PSR template.
Riley: Running `kubectl exec` into scaler pod to inspect state; looks like leader pod in a crashloop for scale attempts. Dumping last 200 lines:
```
E scaler/leader.go: failed to reconcile: provider.ClientError: quota_exceeded
W scaler/leader.go: entering backoff (attempt 4)
I scaler/leader.go: current_nodes=80, desired_nodes=120
```
Riley: Important: config says scale_limit=80 in production for eu-west. That prevented desired_nodes from being honored. I'm pushing a temporary config bump to 120 on the leader. Patching now.
Alex: Patch acknowledged./cc @OpsBot can you kick a manual provisioning request to the provider for 20 extra gpus while we wait for autoscaler to reconcile?
OpsBot: Manual provisioning request queued. Provider ticket #PR-19834 opened. ETA 12-18m.
Mira: I'm also ejecting a few long-lived sessions from the scheduler (force-graceful-evict) for sessions flagged as non-critical. This will free up 6 GPUs. Note: evicting may cause a few in-flight requests to error — marking them as retryable.
Alex: Rolling admission control script to block non-prod and low-priority embeddings now:
```
PATCH /v1/routes/admission
body: {"throttle_rules": [{"tenant":"*_nonprod","rate_limit":5}]}
```
Sam: CS note: initial customer-impact check shows 3 customers with elevated errors (partner-x, retailer-beta, internal-test). Error mode: 429 / 503 from API. Errors spiked 01:56 UTC, persisted until mitigations.
Elaine: Drafting advisory: short summary + ETA for fix, link to status page. Will hold for final approval from Alex.
Riley: Autoscaler leader accepted config bump. It immediately attempted scale_up but provider still 429; new attempt shows progress: desired_nodes=120, provisioning in-flight for 16 nodes.
```
2026-03-15T02:08:12Z scaler: desired_nodes=120
2026-03-15T02:08:14Z provider: allocation accepted (16 nodes) ticket PR-19834
```
Mira: Freeing KV cache and rotating hot GPUs: we moved a few critical sessions to `eu-central` fallback pool to relieve pinned memory. That dropped queue depth by ~45%.
Alex: Good. OpsBot, any provider update?
OpsBot: Provider PR-19834: 4 nodes up (03:06 UTC), 12 pending, no further throttles reported from provider. Expected to stabilize by +25m.
Sam: Customer support: partner-x says some long-running jobs failed but they re-tried and progress resumed. No SLA breach flagged yet — still tracking.
Riley: Observability: token latency median improved after eviction and route changes. Queue depth trending down to 2.1k. Reject rate down to 8%.
Alex: Putting the incident into 'mitigated' state but keeping oncall for monitoring. Summary of immediate mitigations:
- temporary scale_limit bump 80 -> 120 (Riley)
- manual provisioning request PR-19834 (OpsBot)
- forced eviction of non-critical long-lived sessions (Mira)
- admission control for non-prod tenants (Alex)
- failover routing for identified high-SLA tenants to eu-central (Mira)
- customer advisory drafted (Elaine)
Riley: Post-incident quick notes: root cause appears to be two factors combining:
1) sudden tenant-driven queue growth (partner-x batch run) which caused sustained GPU pinning
2) autoscaler enforced hard scale_limit that prevented reacting to surge while provider rate-limited allocation attempts (429s)
Alex: Impact window estimated: 01:55 - 02:11 UTC. Peak reject rate 41% at 01:57. Affected customers: partner-x (high), retailer-beta (medium), internal-test (low). No confirmed SLA credit yet; CS to verify.
Elaine: I'll run impact matrix and list of affected tenant IDs. Will open support threads.
Jen: Platform follow-ups: we should consider increasing default regional scale_limit or implement adaptive emergency scale_limit that ignores some policy during provider ack windows. Also add logic for autoscaler to detect provider 429 vs quota errors and escalate faster to oncall+provider.
Mira: Runtime follow-ups: add better session TTLs and eviction heuristics for long-lived KV cache sessions and rate-limit heavy embedding jobs per tenant.
Riley: Ops follow-ups: add an automated fallback that can route a percentage of traffic to other regions when regional allocation stalls for >2m.
Alex: Action items added — I'll create a postmortem ticket and assign owners:
- PMF-1001 Postmortem write-up (Alex)
- Autoscaler: emergency-scale_limit feature & 429 handling (Riley)
- Runtime: session TTLs + eviction policy (Mira)
- Platform: cross-region fallback automation (Jen)
- CS: customer impact and communication (Elaine)
- Ops: provider incident follow-up & SLA (Ops)
Sam: Quick note for the postmortem: capture the exact tenant payload that triggered this and include workload reproducer if possible.
Riley: Captured sampling of partner-x request headers and job metadata (saved to /var/triage/6372001111/). Will attach to PMF-1001.
Alex: Thanks team. I'll keep the thread open for any late regressions. If anything spikes above 10% rejects, we re-open paging. Great coordination :thumbsup:
Elaine: Preparing final comms now. ETA 20m.
OpsBot: Incident log closed to active paging; status = mitigated. Incident ID INC-6372 recorded.
Alex: Leaving a short timeline for the postmortem body (to copy into PMF-1001):
- 01:54 UTC: partner-x starts large batch embedding job
- 01:55 UTC: queue depth rising; autoscaler starts attempts
- 01:57 UTC: provider returns 429s; autoscaler hits scale_limit=80
- 02:00 UTC: non-prod admission control applied; evictions begin
- 02:06 UTC: config bumped, manual provider request PR-19834 opened
- 02:10 UTC: first new nodes online; queue begins to drain
- 02:11 UTC: reject rate falls below 10%
- 02:16 UTC: mitigation confirmed; incident marked mitigated
Riley: I'll add logs and metrics links to the PMF ticket. /cc @Jen for platform notes.
Jen: Noted. I'll schedule a follow-up sync to discuss changing default scale_limit and a safe escalation policy with provider.
Mira: Adding that we should also expose tenant-level backpressure signals to customers so they can self-throttle large batch runs. Might reduce blast radius.
Alex: Ok wrapping. We'll meet 48h for postmortem review. Thanks everyone, great response.
